text:
JJ Peterka is 25 games into his Bruins life and the line reads 6 goals and 16 points, a touch behind the 47-point pace he set in Utah last season. The finishing is the gap. He has 6 goals on 8.1 expected goals (the quality of his chances), and his shooting sits at 11.5% against a league average of 13.5%. That reads like a scorer waiting on the bounces, not one who has lost it. Ty Anderson of 98.5 The Sports Hub put it simply: "Every time JJ Peterka shoots, you're reminded why he should shoot more."

The engine is still there. He ranks in the 94th percentile for bursts over 20 mph, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him leaving the defensive zone with possession on 59% of his exits last season. The last ten games have been thin (2 goals, 5 points, four games without a shot on goal), but he played 20 and 21.9 minutes in the last two. Our range for his season lands between 44 and 65 points. We'd watch the shot count before the goal count.
